purpose: Test whether explicitly recorded partial measurement slices plus replayable quality or anomaly decisions support long-running measurement advice before live control, scan mutation, or autonomous calibration exists.

user_refinement: measurement-time feedback should be method-aware, replayable, explicitly recorded, and non-intrusive
experiment code should record data, sweep semantics, lifecycle events, and decision-relevant context into Scopecat
prompt_method_check: blind role-play suggested passive advisory feedback over framework replacement
external_baseline: existing frameworks already cover acquisition, plotting, callbacks, dashboards, scheduling, or calibration in their own stacks

artifacts.role: explicitly recorded partial sweep slices and lifecycle events
recorded-input replay check for the same decision packet

fixture_questions: Can explicit partial-sweep recording produce useful decision evidence before a full live-advisory product exists?
Which data slice is complete enough for a quality or anomaly decision?
Can the same decision be replayed from recorded inputs?
What remains advisory evidence rather than hardware, scan, or parameter authority?
